title: Condition 3D fracture populations on measured surface intensity
description: Explore and implement a defensible workflow that generates 3D fracture populations conditioned on observed 2D trace-network intensity. The 2D traces are random planar cuts through 3D fractures, not fracture-plane centers, so do not anchor 3D centers to trace midpoints. Surface intensity (sum trace lengths / target area) may be compared with 3D-network intersections on horizontal slices at selected depths (e.g. 1 m and 10 m). Clarify estimators, stationarity assumptions, edge/domain effects, sampling/conditioning procedure, acceptance tolerances and validation before committing to production behavior; exploratory details can evolve with implementation evidence. Include focused experiments and tests.

title: Diagnose current 3D generator against surface P21 across depth
description: Diagnose the current 3D generator against observed surface P21 and trace count before changing generation parameters. Use the existing Network-to-PorePy exporter with its current per-set orientation/length resampling and cuboid-uniform centers; evaluate without meshing using the pure analytic CSV horizontal-slice helper. Reproducibly evaluate 100 candidate populations at N=60 and N=240, then use the observed zmax hit fraction to estimate/report the total N needed for the extrapolated full-domain top count target. At five evenly spaced sections over z=zmin+10%-90%*height, compute P21 from total circular-fracture chord length clipped to the full rectangular footprint / rectangular footprint area; compare with observed clipped trace length / mapped polygon area (different support is intentional). At zmax, count distinct generated fracture disks with a non-empty section chord; target = 240 * rectangular footprint area / mapped polygon area (KB7 approximately 575). Report per-candidate section errors, top-hit count distributions, and relationship between N and both metrics. Do not anchor centers at observed trace midpoints; do not change exporter parameters or implement production rejection/conditioning during baseline. Keep results exploratory and note assumptions/limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Pure helper tested on analytic circular-disk intersections, offsets, orientation and cuboid clipping; no meshing required. For fixed seeded candidates, report P21 at five interior sections, top zmax fracture-hit count, and candidate variability for N=60 and N=240; report extrapolated zmax target using mapped-polygon-to-rectangular-area ratio, and estimate N needed to reach it under current sampling. P21 relative-error score may report <=20% benchmark as provisional; do not use a hard pass/fail for the count until its tolerance is agreed. No generator behavior changes. Run focused tests and prek.
notes: Prototype conditioning success: keeping base uniform-center generator, add a separate top-surface subset with centers set to zmax to meet extrapolated count exactly, then assess interior P21 (no trace-midpoint anchoring). In 20 seed trials each: base N=2000 reached both 50% criteria in 20/20, median interior P21 relative error 34.7%, total N median 2473; base N=3000 passed 20/20, median P21 error 9.8%, total N median 3424; base N=4000 passed 20/20, median error 24.1%, total N median 4369. The crude top-up fractures also affect interior slices; remain explicitly non-stationary. A 3000-base fixed seed KB7 smoke candidate added 434 top-surface fractures, total 3434, exact 575 zmax hits, mean interior P21 relative error 3.9%, passed relaxed 50% tolerances. Provisional workflow: choose a base count then add top-intersecting fractures; user-defined 50% tolerances and max attempts currently available. No production notebook integration yet; next assess whether user expects editable inputs/tolerances and implement minimal demo if approved.

title: Export seeded random circular fractures from a Network into PorePy 3D CSV
description: After 861 and zud close, implement one public exporter in fractopo/interop/porepy.py, with unit tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. Suggested name: export_network_to_porepy_3d_csv_format; choose an equally explicit established-style name only if necessary. Inputs: a fractopo.analysis.network.Network, positive integer fracture_count, cuboid bounds in exact order (xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax), and optional numpy.random.Generator. No integer seed overload and no global np.random state. Reuse 861 extraction. Given usable sets in Network.azimuth_set_names order, compute quotas with largest-remainder allocation: raw = proportion * fracture_count; take floors; allocate remaining count(s) to greatest fractional remainder; resolve equal remainders by original azimuth_set_names order. This guarantees exact total and deterministic quotas. For each quota, empirical-resample a valid row with replacement using rng.choice; sample centre components independently with rng.uniform(xmin, xmax), rng.uniform(ymin, ymax), rng.uniform(zmin, zmax). Use sampled trace azimuth as geological strike (degrees to radians) and sampled dip (degrees to radians); PorePy right-hand rule implies dip direction, so v1 neither reads nor emits dip direction. Create circular EllipticalFracture values: axis=sampled trace length / 2 and major_axis_angle=0. Return a string whose first row is the six-value cuboid domain, followed by one eight-field row per generated fracture. The function need not call a separate CSV validator. Guarantee centres only, not disk containment. Validate finite strictly increasing bounds and count > 0 before sampling. No PorePy import/dependency, parametric distribution sampling, or new configuration classes.
acceptance_criteria: With a seeded numpy.random.default_rng passed twice, identical input yields byte-identical CSV. Tests prove domain is the first six-field line; each later row parses to eight finite numeric fields with equal positive axes; exact output row count equals fracture_count; quota allocation uses usable observation count and largest-remainder/original-name tie break; sampled axis is one half of a valid source length; strike is a source azimuth in radians; dip is a source dip in radians; every centre lies inside supplied bounds; invalid count/bounds fail clearly. Test manual and automatic set labels through 861 extraction. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.
